title: Late Breaking Results: Modern Automatic PCB Placement with Complex Constraints
problem: Existing PCB placement fails to address complex constraints such as diverse wire widths, intricate spacing rules, and irregular component shapes. Manual placement requires expertise and is time-consuming.
motivation: Automated PCB placement is needed for large-scale complex designs to handle heterogeneous components, clearance conditions, wire areas, power circuit flow, and routability.
method: The method places components in two stages. First, force-directed global placement (treating components as springs pulling toward ideal positions) uses power circuit anchor points (reference locations derived from power flow requirements) to guide the overall layout. Then simulated annealing (iteratively adjusting positions with gradually decreasing random movements) refines the placement of component pads—the electrical connection points—to satisfy complex spacing rules. Finally, window-based legalization (processing the board in regions) removes overlaps while preserving all spacing constraints.
key_novelty: The approach combines power circuit anchor point guidance with simulated annealing for pad alignment to automatically handle complex PCB spacing constraints.
contributions: Force-directed global placement with power circuit flow consideration
Power circuit anchor point derivation for placement guidance
Simulated annealing-based pad alignment for complex spacing constraints
Window-based legalization handling multiple constraint types
primary_theme: Automated PCB placement with complex constraints
